title: Atrium publication metadata: five open-license sculpture candidates
scope: Object identity, catalog facts, scan-license attribution and non-graphic art-context review. Source thumbnails visually inspected; this is not geometry, texture or final viewer QA.
general_license_note: The public-domain status of the historical sculpture is distinct from the license of a contemporary 3D scan. Keep source model attribution and license linked on the work page; record actual edits and conversions.

works.title: Aphrodite
works.credit_line: Gift of the John Huntington Art and Polytechnic Trust
works.artwork_rights: Public domain; museum marks this work available for copying, modification and distribution without permission.
works.scan_attribution: Aphrodite, 400–200 BCE, Greece. Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of the John Huntington Art and Polytechnic Trust, 1927.489. 3D scan published by the Cleveland Museum of Art under CC0 1.0.
works.attribution_requirement: Credit is not legally required under CC0; retain museum/object provenance as good curatorial practice.
works.description: A small terracotta Aphrodite shifts her weight onto one leg, with her torso following a gentle curve. The museum connects this figure to the famous Aphrodite of Knidos and suggests she may once have held a mirror. The surviving fragments preserve both its intimate scale and its poised movement.
works.content_assessment: Adult mythological female nude; no sexual act. Source thumbnail inspected.
works.identity_assessment: Museum accession, model title, material and image all agree.
works.publication_status: Metadata and source license verified; publish only after model acquisition and geometry/orientation QA.

works.description: Carpeaux places Eve beside the tree in the Garden of Eden, turning the biblical episode into a compact study of gesture and movement. The bronze figure brings a hand toward her mouth as a serpent coils around the support behind her.
works.content_assessment: Adult biblical female nude; no sexual act. Source thumbnail inspected.
works.identity_assessment: Museum object directly linked by museum-published scan; inscription and bronze appearance agree. Use museum date 1874 rather than scan title’s c.1874.
works.publication_status: Metadata and source license verified; publish only after model acquisition and geometry/orientation QA.

works.title: Les Trois Grâces (The Three Graces)
works.dimensions: 82.55 × 46.99 cm (32 1/2 × 18 1/2 in.); museum supplies two dimensions
works.artwork_rights: Public Domain in the museum object API.
works.scan_attribution: 3D scan: Minneapolis Institute of Art (Mia); research led by Michael Tetzlaff, University of Wisconsin–Stout, with Cultural Heritage Imaging and Mia; model building and customization by Lou Brown. Licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.
works.attribution_requirement: Display attribution, model-source link, license link and actual modifications. Keep adapted model files under CC BY-SA 4.0. Do not imply endorsement.
works.description: Three dancing figures link hands in this plaster group related to Carpeaux’s Dance for the Paris Opéra. Raised arms, bent knees and turning bodies carry the eye around the sculpture. Its lively treatment of the female figure reflects the naturalism that made the larger composition controversial.
works.content_assessment: Adult female mythological dancers; no sexual act. Source thumbnail inspected. The principal figures are adults; do not use unrelated Petit Palais variant metadata, which mentions a putto.
works.identity_assessment: Scan’s tinyurl.com/3wvzxfue resolves to Mia object 2224. This is the Mia plaster, not the Musée d’Orsay or Petit Palais object.
works.publication_status: Metadata and source license verified; publish only after model acquisition and geometry/orientation QA.

works.title: Bacchante
works.institution: National Museum in Kraków, Gallery of 19th-Century Polish Art in Sukiennice
works.artwork_rights: Historical artwork from 1887 by an artist who died in 1913; public-domain assessment based on these dates. The model publisher expressly grants CC BY 4.0 for the scan.
works.scan_attribution: 3D digitisation: Regional Digitisation Lab, Małopolska Institute of Culture in Kraków, Poland, “Virtual Museums of Małopolska” Project. Physical sculpture: National Museum in Kraków, Gallery of 19th-Century Polish Art in Sukiennice, MNK II-rz-276. Licensed CC BY 4.0.
works.attribution_requirement: Display the digitization team and project, model-source link, license link and actual modifications. Do not imply endorsement.
works.description: Rygier’s bronze dancer raises a goblet while holding a vine branch, identifying her with the celebrations of Dionysus. Drapery gathers at her hips as her upper body leans into the movement. The detailed sandals and animated expression bring an observed, individual quality to the mythological subject.
works.content_assessment: Adult female mythological dancer with partially draped body; no sexual act. Source thumbnail inspected.
works.identity_assessment: Scan description identifies accession MNK II-rz-276 and Sukiennice collection; museum title, artist, date, material and image agree.
works.publication_status: Metadata and source license verified; publish only after model acquisition and geometry/orientation QA.

works.title: Psyche
works.artist_note: Designed by Rodin; marble carved by professional artisans under his supervision.
works.credit_line: Anonymous gift in memory of Ward Thoron (1867–1938) and Louisa Chapin Hooper Thoron (1874–1975)
works.artwork_rights: French Sculpture Census explicitly lists artist copyright as public domain; 1899 object documented at MFA and Getty CONA.
works.scan_attribution: “Psyche by Auguste Rodin” 3D scan by avi (https://sketchfab.com/avi), captured at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston using Polycam photo mode. Licensed CC BY 4.0.
works.attribution_requirement: Credit avi as scan creator, link the source model and CC BY 4.0, and state actual modifications. Museum object credit is separate; do not imply the scan is institutionally commissioned.
works.description: Psyche leans forward beneath an open cloak, poised as if trying to see her sleeping lover. Rodin sets the softly modeled figure against sweeping folds and a roughly worked marble base. The sculpture was exhibited in Paris in 1900 before entering the collection associated with the MFA.
works.content_assessment: Adult mythological female nude in a narrative moment; no sexual act. Source thumbnail inspected.
works.identity_assessment: Community scan title, museum location and visible composition agree with MFA Psyche, accession 1975.738. Mesh quality still requires acquisition QA; source listing has 46,230 faces.
works.publication_status: Metadata and source license verified; publish only after model acquisition and geometry/orientation QA.
